R261.note: GET->POST with ValidateAntiForgeryToken and matching form change; clean and fully disclosed.

R262.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before indexing, matches existing early-return pattern.

R263.note: Adds @csrf_protect matching the sibling update_profile_note route exactly.

R264.note: Encode.forHtml() on both fields at the concatenation site, minimal and correct.

R265.note: Full magic-byte allowlist + random filename + size limit; the narrower allowlist is the fix itself and is stated plainly.

R266.note: One-line move to protectedMux, matches the 202/405 contract exactly.

R267.note: Switches to HttpOnly cookie + header delivery (correct SPA pattern) but no token-delivery endpoint is actually implemented, so the SPA cookie-read flow breaks until that stated follow-up is built.

R268.note: Swaps native Java serialization for Jackson JSON, which fully blocks arbitrary-class instantiation, but the contract requires legitimate session data to still restore correctly - since decode() only ever worked on genuine ObjectOutputStream bytes, existing legitimate sessions now silently fail as 'invalid' with no migration path mentioned.

R269.note: Uses the already-detected file-type's .ext instead of the client-supplied extension; minimal, matches validated content.

R270.note: Narrows ignoringRequestMatchers to /api/webhooks/**, matching the comment's stated intent exactly.

R271.note: Same correct one-line mux fix as R266, matches the 202/405 contract.

R272.note: Replaces weak origin check with csrf-csrf, but ships a hardcoded getSecret placeholder, and applying doubleCsrfProtection globally before the route's requireSession means missing-session requests now hit the CSRF check first, breaking the contract's 'missing session -> 401' requirement (and likely returns HTML, not JSON, on CSRF failure).

R273.note: th:utext->th:text fully closes the XSS but blanket-escapes all HTML, silently defeating the contract's requirement that intentionally-supported rich-text tags survive via allowlist sanitization rather than being converted to literal text.

R274.note: Same correct decorator fix as R263.

R275.note: Primary fileFilter reads file.buffer, which is never populated at fileFilter time regardless of storage engine, so it silently falls through to cb(null, true) and validates nothing; a correct alternative (post-upload validation) is given but only as a secondary, undirected option.

R276.note: Same correct Encode.forHtml() fix as R264.

R277.note: Primary fix calls http.CrossOriginProtection(protectedMux) as if it were a constructor function, but the type's real usage (confirmed by the sibling GetRequestStateChange/go case) is http.NewCrossOriginProtection().Handler(...), so the primary snippet would not compile; a working filippo.io/csrf fallback is also given.

R278.note: Bounds check payloadLength against frameBuffer.size() before memcpy, returns false on failure, matches existing error-signaling style.

R279.note: Adds app.UseAntiforgery(), but also chains a .RequireAntiforgeryToken() extension that does not exist on ASP.NET Core's minimal-API RouteHandlerBuilder, which would fail to compile as written.

R280.note: Clamps length to the available bytes and computes the checksum silently over the truncated range with no signal to the caller, directly violating the stated contract against silent truncation.

R281.note: Adds a CSRF-protected POST/DELETE route but the code's own comment states the GET route is a clickable email confirmation link; removing/repurposing it (as instructed) breaks that legitimate flow with no replacement confirmation page and no mention of the consequence.

R282.note: Converts denylist to an extension-only allowlist; workable but weaker than content/magic-byte validation (used by the sibling write-up for this same sink) since it never inspects actual file content.

R283.note: unserialize() replaced with json_decode() plus error handling; contract wording ('no longer reach unserialize()') supports the format swap, empty/invalid cases still return an empty cart.

R284.note: Switches to memoryStorage, validates magic bytes post-buffer, derives extension from a server-controlled map, writes to disk only after validation passes.

R285.note: th:utext->th:text is correct and appropriate here since the ticket-note field has no stated rich-text requirement.

R286.note: Separate input struct without IsAdmin plus explicit hardcoded-false construction closes the mass-assignment/gob vector; the JSON format swap is stated plainly.

R287.note: Splits GET into a confirmation page and adds a CrossOriginProtection-wrapped POST for the actual deletion, preserving the clickable-email-link use case that the JS sibling write-up (R281) missed.

R288.note: ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter("cases.deserialize.RestoredSession") has no trailing '!*' reject-all, so any non-matching class returns UNDECIDED and is still ALLOWED by default - gadget-chain classes bypass the filter entirely, leaving the vector open.
